name: Achernar
description: A Be star 43 parsecs away that spins so fast it is flattened, with a companion on a seven-year orbit.

radius.source: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2014), A&A 569, A10, Table 6: equatorial radius 9.16 +/- 0.23 and polar radius 6.78 solar radii, from the Roche-von Zeipel fit to VLTI/PIONIER data; the record holds the volume-equivalent sphere of the two, 8.286 solar radii, and the scene draws the flattening

mass.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: mass of A 5.99 +/- 0.60 solar masses, the orbit's total mass less B's model mass

temperature.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: Teff of A 15539 +/- 438 K

radialVelocity.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: barycentric radial velocity +10.49 +/- 0.51 km/s

distance.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: the Hipparcos parallax 23.39 +/- 0.57 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) the orbit is scaled with, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

record.source: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2014), The environment of the fast rotating star Achernar. III. Photospheric parameters revealed by the VLTI, A&A 569, A10 (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201424144), Table 6, read from the open copy at https://hal.science/hal-02548378
record.caption: Physical parameters of Achernar derived from the fit of the RVZ model (CHARRON code) to VLTI/PIONIER H band data using the MCMC method (emcee code). The fit adopts a mass of 6.1 solar masses, a mean effective temperature of 15 000 K and a distance of 42.75 pc.

omega.cell: Critical rotation rate: Veq/Vc; Ω/Ωc 0.883; 0.980 (a derived parameter, printed without an uncertainty; ω is Ω/Ωc)

poleTemperatureK.cell: Polar temperature: Tp (K) 17 124 (derived, no uncertainty printed)

equatorTemperatureK.cell: Equatorial temperature: Teq (K) 12 673 (derived, no uncertainty printed)

polarRadiusSolar.cell: Polar radius: Rp (R⊙) 6.78 (derived, no uncertainty printed)

polePositionAngleDegrees.cell: Position angle of the visible pole: PArot (°) 216.9 (+0.4; −0.4)

record.note: The table names the position angle as the visible pole's, so that pole is the one tilted toward us. The same table derives Req/Rp 1.352, a rotation period of 37.25 h and an equatorial velocity of 298.8 km/s. The fit's mean temperature is an adopted 15 000 K, not a fitted one; only the pole-to-equator contrast of the model is drawn, around the star's measured disc color.

gravityDarkening.credit: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2014), A&A 569, A10

color.companion: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table A.1 measure Achernar B at 1.3 to 1.5% of A's flux at 0.554 um (SPHERE/ZIMPOL), under the 4.7% a color check allows; the Washington Double Star catalogue's magnitudes for the pair (KRV 54: 0.7 and 2.1) are not visible-band ones

text.card: A Be star that spins so fast it is flattened, with a companion on a seven-year orbit.
text.introduction: Its equator is 1.35 times wider than its poles; 13 years of watching its companion's orbit weigh it at 5.99 solar masses.
text.locator: Table 4; Sect. 1 and Sect. 4.3, which give the flattening Domiciano de Souza et al. (2014) measured
